name: Kiruna mine
note: Iron ore mine operating since 1898. The Per Geijer rare earth and phosphate resource announced in 2023 is the largest known REE deposit in the EU, but is not in production.
crma_project: ReeMAP Project: Malmberget, Per Geijer and Luleå Industrial Park

name: Aitik mine
note: One of the largest open-pit copper mines in Europe.

name: Rönnskär smelter
note: Copper smelter with a dedicated arsenic plant.

name: Rönnskär e-scrap recovery
note: Among the largest electronic scrap recycling operations in Europe.

name: Nunasvaara / Vittangi graphite
note: High-grade graphite project intended to feed a Lulea anode refinery. Permitting has been protracted.

name: Woxna graphite mine
note: Built in the 1990s, on care and maintenance pending anode-grade qualification.

name: Norra Kärr REE project
note: Unusually heavy-enriched rare earth deposit. Permitting contested for over a decade.

name: ReeMAP rare earth plant
note: Planned processing of mine tailings into rare earth and phosphate products.
crma_project: ReeMAP Project: Malmberget, Per Geijer and Luleå Industrial Park

name: Terrafame mine and bioleaching plant
note: Bioheapleaching operation with an on-site battery chemicals plant.

name: Kevitsa mine
note: Open-pit nickel-copper-PGM mine.

name: Harjavalta smelter
note: Copper and nickel smelting on a shared industrial site.

name: Harjavalta nickel refinery
note: The EU’s largest nickel refinery. Ownership and feed sourcing have been under review since 2022.

name: Kokkola cobalt refinery
note: One of the largest cobalt refineries outside China. Ownership has changed repeatedly: Outokumpu, then OM Group, then Freeport Cobalt, then Jervois. Verify the current operator.
crma_project: Jervois Finland Cobalt Refinery Expansion Project

name: Keliber lithium mine
note: Spodumene mining feeding the Kokkola refinery.

name: Keliber lithium hydroxide refinery
note: Intended to be one of the first integrated EU lithium hydroxide plants.

name: Siilinjärvi mine
note: The only phosphate rock mine in the European Union.

name: Nikkelverk refinery
note: Major European nickel and cobalt refinery, also recovering PGMs.

name: Herøya rare earth separation
note: Separation plant using a solvent extraction alternative, aimed at magnet-grade oxides.

name: Porsgrunn manganese plant
note: Refined manganese alloys.

name: Sauda manganese plant
note: Manganese ferroalloy smelter.

name: Kvinesdal manganese plant
note: Silicomanganese production.

name: Skaland graphite mine
note: Among the highest-grade natural graphite mines in the world, and the only one operating in Europe.

name: Fen carbonatite REE project
note: Large carbonatite-hosted rare earth resource announced in 2024.

name: Salten silicon plant
note: Silicon metal furnaces.

name: Thamshavn silicon plant
note: Silicon metal with energy recovery.

name: Årdal aluminium plant
note: Hydropower-based primary aluminium.

name: Sunndal aluminium plant
note: One of the largest primary aluminium plants in Europe.

name: Aurubis Hamburg
note: The largest copper smelter in Europe.

name: Trimet Hamburg
note: Primary aluminium smelter.

name: Trimet Essen
note: Primary aluminium smelter and group headquarters.

name: Aurubis Lünen
note: Secondary copper smelter processing complex recycling feed.

name: AMG Lithium Bitterfeld
note: Lithium hydroxide refinery, the first of its kind in Germany.

name: Vulcan geothermal lithium
note: Lithium extraction from geothermal brine in the Upper Rhine Graben, with no conventional mine.

name: Zinnwald lithium project
note: Historic tin-tungsten district being redeveloped for lithium mica. Zinnwald Lithium was acquired outright by AMG Critical Materials in July 2026, which has begun an 18-24 month review of the project scope.

name: Wacker Burghausen
note: Polysilicon and silicones. One of the largest polysilicon producers outside China.

name: Heraeus Hanau
note: Precious metals refining and recycling.

name: Clara mine
note: Baryte and fluorspar mine in the Black Forest.

name: Umicore Hoboken
note: One of the largest complex-metals recycling plants in the world, recovering a long list of by-product metals.

name: Umicore Olen
note: Cobalt and germanium refining and specialty materials.

name: Aurubis Olen
note: Copper rod and shapes.

name: Aurubis Beerse
note: Multi-metal recycler, formerly Metallo.

name: Campine Beerse
note: Antimony trioxide from recycled feed, a rare non-Chinese source.

name: Solvay La Rochelle
note: Long-established rare earth separation plant, and one of only two in the EU.

name: Framatome Jarrie
note: Zirconium and hafnium separation. France is the leading world producer of hafnium.

name: Nyrstar Auby
note: Zinc smelter recovering germanium and indium from residues.

name: Aluminium Dunkerque
note: The largest primary aluminium smelter in the European Union.

name: EMILI lithium project
note: Underground lithium mica project at an existing kaolin operation.

name: Neves-Corvo mine
note: Major Iberian Pyrite Belt copper and zinc mine.
crma_project: Lombador North Phase 2, Semblana and 3rd SILO

name: Panasqueira mine
note: Tungsten mine worked continuously for over a century. Operated by Beralt Tin and Wolfram, a subsidiary of Almonty Industries.

name: Mina do Barroso
note: The most advanced hard-rock lithium project in the EU. Locally contested.

name: Aljustrel mine
note: Zinc and copper in the Iberian Pyrite Belt.

name: Atlantic Copper Huelva
note: Copper smelter and refinery, with a new recycling plant alongside.

name: Riotinto mine
note: Historic copper district restarted in 2015.

name: Cobre Las Cruces
note: Open pit with a hydrometallurgical plant; transitioning to an underground polymetallic project.

name: Barruecopardo mine
note: Open-pit tungsten mine reopened in 2019. Saloro S.L.U. is wholly owned by EQ Resources.

name: Penouta mine
note: Tantalum, niobium and tin recovered from the tailings of a historic mine. The EU’s only notable tantalum source. Previous operator Strategic Minerals Spain collapsed in 2024 and halted production that October; Energy Transition Minerals acquired the rights and restarted the mine in July 2026.

name: Asturias fluorspar operations
note: One of the largest fluorspar producers in western Europe. Exact site names and status should be verified.

name: San José lithium project
note: Lithium mica project close to the city of Cáceres. Locally contested.

name: San Ciprián alumina and aluminium
note: Alumina refinery and smelter. The smelter was curtailed in 2021 over energy costs. Alcoa and IGNIS EQT formed a joint venture in March 2025 (Alcoa 75%, managing operator) and the smelter restart ran through 2025 and 2026, reaching full capacity around mid-2026.

name: Sabón silicon plant
note: Silicon metal and ferroalloys.

name: Puertollano silicon plant
note: Silicon metal furnaces.

name: Mittersill tungsten mine
note: The largest tungsten mine in the European Union.

name: St. Martin tungsten plant
note: Tungsten carbide powder production and scrap recycling.

name: Montanwerke Brixlegg
note: Secondary copper smelter running entirely on recycled feed.

name: Treibacher Althofen
note: Ferroalloys and specialty chemicals, including vanadium recovery from spent catalysts.

name: Wolfsberg lithium project
note: Underground spodumene project in Carinthia.

name: Cínovec lithium project
note: One of the largest hard-rock lithium resources in Europe, straddling the German border.

name: Global Tungsten and Powders Bruntál
note: Tungsten powder and carbide production.

name: Karviná coking coal mines
note: The last operating hard coal mines in Czechia, with closure scheduled.

name: Lubin mine
note: Part of the Legnica-Głogów copper belt, Europe’s largest copper mining district.

name: Głogów smelter
note: Copper smelter also recovering rhenium and precious metals.

name: Legnica smelter
note: Copper smelter and refinery.

name: JSW coking coal mines
note: The largest coking coal producer in the European Union.

name: Odolanów helium plant
note: Helium separated from domestic natural gas. The only significant EU source.

name: Bauxite mines
note: Greece is the largest bauxite producer in the European Union.

name: Alumina and aluminium plant
note: The only integrated alumina refinery and aluminium smelter in the EU.

name: Larymna ferronickel plant
note: Ferronickel from domestic laterite ore. The company entered insolvency proceedings and operating status has been unstable. Verify before relying on this row.

name: Aurubis Bulgaria
note: Copper smelter and refinery.

name: Chelopech mine
note: Underground copper-gold mine. Dundee Precious Metals renamed itself DPM Metals in September 2025.

name: Alro Slatina
note: One of the largest aluminium smelters in central Europe.

name: Slovalco
note: Primary aluminium production halted in 2022 over energy costs and restarted on 28 August 2026, initially at about 75,000 t/y against a full capacity of 175,000 t/y.

name: Neo Performance Materials Silmet
note: Rare earth separation, and one of only two such plants in the EU. A magnet plant has been added on the same site.

name: Orani feldspar quarry
note: Sardinian feldspar for the ceramics industry. Site name and operator should be verified.

name: Bor copper complex
note: Historic Serbian copper district, majority acquired by Zijin in 2018.

name: Bor smelter
note: Copper smelter and refinery on the same complex.

name: Jadar project
note: Jadarite contains both lithium and boron. Licences were revoked in 2022 and reinstated in 2024 amid sustained protest.

name: Zavalivsky graphite mine
note: One of the few operating graphite mines in Europe. Operations affected by the war.

name: Kırka borate mine
note: Part of the largest borate reserve base in the world.

name: Bandırma boron plant
note: Boric acid and refined borate products.

name: Grundartangi smelter
note: Geothermal and hydro powered aluminium.

name: Fjarðaál smelter
note: Hydropower-based primary aluminium.

name: Bakki silicon plant
note: Geothermally powered silicon metal. Production was temporarily suspended from mid-July 2025 over silicon market conditions; PCC SE says it intends to restart when prices recover.

name: Less Common Metals
note: Rare earth metal and alloy production for permanent magnets, one of very few outside Asia.

name: Cornish Lithium projects
note: Lithium from geothermal brine and hard rock in Cornwall.

name: 9-Tech photovoltaic recovery
note: Recovers silicon, glass, cobalt, lithium and neodymium from end-of-life photovoltaic panels, batteries, circuit boards and magnets. A prototype line runs; the company reports building permits granted in May 2025 for a 4,500 t/year plant.

name: cylib recycling plant
note: Spin-off of RWTH Aachen recovering lithium and graphite alongside the usual nickel and cobalt from black mass.

name: tozero black mass plant
note: Hydrometallurgical recovery of lithium and graphite from black mass, at the Gendorf chemical park in Burghausen. Munich is the company’s registered office, not the plant.

name: HyProMag magnet recycling
note: University of Birmingham spin-out using hydrogen processing to recover NdFeB magnet alloy from end-of-life magnets.

name: Ionic Technologies demonstration plant
note: Queen’s University Belfast spin-out separating rare earth oxides from magnet scrap.

name: Altilium ACT recycling
note: Recovers battery cathode metals from end-of-life electric vehicle packs.

name: Hydrovolt battery recycling
note: One of the larger European battery recycling plants, producing black mass alongside aluminium and plastics.

name: Librec battery recycling
note: Full-cycle lithium-ion battery recycling.

name: Mecaware pilot
note: Carbon dioxide based route to battery metal recovery. Early stage; verify scale and status before relying on this row.

name: Caremag rare earth plant
note: Rare earth refining and magnet recycling project, intended to add a second separation site in France alongside La Rochelle.

name: Green Lithium refinery
note: Planned merchant lithium refinery on Teesside, taking concentrate from third-party mines.

name: Ageli
note: Geothermal brine lithium in Alsace. The CRM Act annex gives the Member State only; the town here is inferred and should be checked.

name: Aguablanca
note: Nickel-copper-PGM deposit in Extremadura, on care and maintenance since 2016 and now a designated Strategic Project.

name: Alpha Project
note: Platinum group metal recycling. The CRM Act annex gives the Member State only; the town here is inferred and should be checked.

name: BAM4EVER (Phase I & II)
note: Battery-grade graphite processing in Savoie.

name: Chvaletice Manganese Project
note: High-purity manganese from the tailings of a historic pyrite mine — reprocessing waste rather than opening new ground.

name: CirCular
note: Recovery of copper, nickel and platinum group metals from electronic scrap, alongside the existing smelter.

name: CO2Graphite
note: Battery-grade graphite synthesised from captured carbon dioxide.

name: GALLICAM
note: Battery cathode material precursors at the Sandouville nickel refinery.

name: Hycamite graphite plant
note: Splits methane into hydrogen and solid battery-grade graphite.

name: Orano Batteries hydrometallurgy
note: Black mass hydrometallurgy at Dunkirk.

name: Las Navas
note: Lithium project in Extremadura. The CRM Act annex gives the Member State only; the town here is inferred and should be checked.

name: INSPIREE
note: Rare earth recovery for magnets. The CRM Act annex gives the Member State only; the town here is inferred and should be checked.

name: Lift One
note: Lithium chemicals plant on the Estarreja chemical complex.

name: Lithium Hydroxide Converter Guben
note: Merchant lithium hydroxide converter taking imported spodumene.

name: MagFactory
note: Recycles end-of-life magnets straight back into new magnets, skipping separation.

name: Mina Doade
note: Lithium project in Galicia. The CRM Act annex gives the Member State only; the town here is inferred and should be checked.

name: El Moto
note: Tungsten project in Ciudad Real.

name: NorthCYCLE
note: Listed as ongoing in the March 2025 annex. Northvolt entered insolvency in 2025. Lyten agreed in March 2026 to acquire the Revolt site and expected to close in Q2 2026; completion is not confirmed here, so the operator is left as recorded and the status stays uncertain.

name: POLVOLT
note: Battery and catalyst recycling at Zawiercie in Silesia. Grodzisk Mazowiecki is the group’s original plant and head office, not the POLVOLT site.

name: Portovesme CRM Hub
note: Conversion of the Sardinian lead-zinc smelter into a black mass processing hub.

name: ProHiPerSi
note: Silicon anode material intended to substitute for battery-grade graphite. The CRM Act annex gives the Member State only; the town here is inferred and should be checked.

name: Fortum Hydromet
note: Hydrometallurgical battery recycling on the Harjavalta industrial site.

name: Puławy Rare Earths Separation Plant
note: Would be one of very few rare earth separation plants in the EU.

name: ReGAIN
note: Substitution of germanium. The CRM Act annex gives the Member State only; the town here is inferred and should be checked.

name: Romano Mine
note: Hard-rock lithium project in northern Portugal.

name: Rovina Valley
note: Copper-gold porphyry project in Hunedoara county.

name: Sakatti
note: Copper-nickel-PGM deposit beneath a protected mire, which has shaped the permitting debate.

name: SALROM Baia de Fier
note: Graphite deposit in Gorj county, held by the state salt and minerals company.

name: Verde Magnesium
note: Would be the first primary magnesium metal production in the EU since 2001.

name: Viridian Lithium
note: Lithium conversion plant in Alsace.

name: RECOVER-IT
note: Plant at Cadoneghe, in the province of Padua.

name: P6 Metals (La Parrilla)
note: Reopening of the historic La Parrilla deposit for tungsten and tin. Tin is not on the EU critical raw materials list, so only tungsten is ticked here.
